turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, Mrs. Iyer, have a seat. What brings you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, I feel tired all the time, and I get breathless, and my periods are very heavy since one year. Is this something serious? I have been worrying a lot.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will take it step by step. Since when have you been this tired?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That I cannot date, doctor. Maybe a few months, maybe it started along with the periods last year, I truly don't remember. Even after sleeping the whole night I feel drained, and if I stand up quickly I feel giddy. Will I faint one day?
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you actually fainted?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I have not fainted. It is only a light feeling, then it passes.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the breathlessness, when does that come on?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): When I climb to our flat, it is the second floor, or if I walk fast for the bus. Sitting quietly I am fine. Doctor, is my heart becoming weak?
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): I would not call the heart weak from the story alone. Any chest pain along with the breathlessness?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no chest pain at all.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any swelling in the feet, or palpitations, the heart racing?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Feet are not swollen. Um, sometimes the heart beats fast when I am very tired... well, actually, no, I would not call it palpitations. It is more just the exhaustion.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, we will leave palpitations aside. Tell me about the periods in ordinary words, how heavy they are.

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): They are very heavy since one year. I go through so many pads that I lose count, many in a day, and there are big clots, quite big, though I cannot say the size. Could it be a tumour inside?
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not calling it a tumour from this chair. How many days does the bleeding last now?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Seven or eight days, and sometimes it drags on even more. Earlier it used to finish in four days only.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you get pain or cramps with it?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, cramps on the first two days. I take Crocin for that, the pain-and-fever tablet, one tablet when the cramp comes. If I take it every month, will my kidneys get spoiled?
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Crocin is paracetamol, and one tablet for the cramp, within what the strip says, is generally safe for the kidneys. Are you on any other tablets?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): The red iron tablets, for the blood. I take them sometimes only, when I remember, not daily. A neighbour said they cause constipation, so I skip them. Is that the reason I am still so weak?
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse read your medication list just now, and she has put down ferrous sulphate 200 mg twice a day.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, that is not right. I never take it twice. I think the tablet is 100 mg, the small red one, but I am not sure of the number. Has she mixed my paper with another patient's?
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): We should not settle the strength from memory. Kindly bring the strip when you come next. Separately, have you noticed hair fall?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, a lot of hair comes away in the shower, since some months. My mother says thyroid is there in our family, her sister is taking thyroid tablets. Do you think I also have thyroid, and is that why the hair is falling?
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will note thyroid disease in your mother's sister. Has your weight gone up or down?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, the weight is the same, as far as I know. I have not checked on a scale.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): How are the bowels, and passing urine?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Motions are normal. There is no burning when I pass urine. I am vegetarian, doctor, I hardly eat any greens, and at the bank I sit the whole day. Can a poor diet make the blood this low?
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): A low-greens diet can contribute, yes. Do you smoke, or take any alcohol?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked, and I don't take alcohol. Am I troubling you with all these small questions?
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not at all, it helps. Any operation in the past, or diabetes, or high blood pressure?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No operation ever. No diabetes and no high BP. I was quite alright until these periods became heavy.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me examine you now. Pulse is 96 per minute, and the blood pressure is 108 over 70. Your palms are pale, the ankles are not swollen, and the chest is clear with no wheeze.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 108 over 70 too low for me? Will I collapse on the stairs going home? And 96 for the pulse, is that a danger sign?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): 108 over 70 is an acceptable pressure, not a collapse figure. A pulse of 96 can fit with the blood being a bit low. I am not finding fluid in the ankles or any wheeze.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So you do think the blood is low. Please say it straight, will I need a blood transfusion? I am really frightened of transfusion.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): No transfusion is being planned. My working impression is iron deficiency from the heavy periods over this past year, and that would join up the tiredness, the breathlessness on climbing, the pale palms, and the hair fall.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Then what about the thyroid my mother spoke of? You have not really answered that, and I keep fearing it is something very bad.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thyroid disease remains on the differential, and I cannot rule it out today. The tests will tell us more than I can by talking.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): What tests, exactly? Will there be many needles, because I get very shaky? My cousin had a scan and then an operation for fibroids, are you going to do that to me?

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am arranging a full blood count, a ferritin level, and a thyroid function test, all from a single draw. No operation is arranged. We might do a pelvic ultrasound only if the bleeding is still this heavy once those results are back, and it is not booked today.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Should I take the red iron tablets every day from tonight? Is it 100 mg or the 200 mg the nurse read? I don't want to take a wrong dose and harm myself.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please do not change the iron until you bring the strip and we have the ferritin. One Crocin when the cramp comes is fine. If you get more breathless, or chest pain, or you feel you are about to faint, come back sooner and do not wait out the week.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): If I stay much the same, when do I see you? Can I keep working at the bank, or should I take leave? And what should I be eating?

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in one week, and bring the reports plus the iron strip. You can continue at the bank, only don't rush for the bus. Try to take some green vegetables on most days.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): One week feels very long if this is serious. If a report is very bad, will somebody call me, or do I only find out here?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): If a result needs urgent action, we will contact you. Otherwise we sit with the numbers together in one week. Let me summarise it back, so we are not missing anything.

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heavy periods for a year, with more pads than you can count and clots you cannot size, tiredness you cannot put a date on, breathlessness on the stairs but not while sitting, no chest pain, no fainting, no swollen feet. Hair fall for some months, red iron tablets only sometimes, which you say is not the nurse's ferrous sulphate 200 mg twice a day, and your mother's sister has thyroid disease. Blood tests today, a pelvic scan only if the bleeding stays this heavy after the results, and I will see you in one week.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that is all correct. I will bring the strip. If the thyroid test is normal, doctor, will my hair grow back?
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hair often improves once the cause is treated, but I will not promise regrowth before the results. We will go over everything in one week.
